# TriviumDB

> TriviumDB brings semantic vector search, native hyperbolic nearest-neighbor search, property graphs, and document evidence into one embedded Rust database. A single TQL query can find nearby embeddings inside a named graph, follow their relationships, and return the records behind the result. Rust, Python, and Node.js run the same storage and query kernel in the host process.

TriviumDB is designed for agent memory, local RAG, and knowledge graphs. A NodeId can carry an embedding, JSON payload, indexed text, and labeled edges. An agent can keep a passage, its embedding, and its links under one identity. Separate database instances can isolate agents, sessions, or tenants.

## Composing retrieval with TQL

Use TQL when the answer depends on both similarity and relationships. For a citation search, an agent can run `SEARCH VECTOR` and return the seed papers' titles, then decide whether to follow their references. To do so, submit a new query with the same search prefix, follow `cites` edges with `EXPAND`, and use `RANK` to score those papers against the original vector. Once the strategy is settled, the host can execute the full pipeline in one call.

`AS` names results and `WITH` passes selected bindings to later stages of the same query. The Cascades planner can combine vector or BM25 retrieval with graph traversal, graph algorithms, filtering, and reranking. Use `EXPLAIN` for plan estimates and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` for observed row counts. [TQL syntax and operators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/tql-reference.md)

## Choose the vector index

- **QuIVer is the default ANN index for dense semantic embeddings.** Use it for cosine retrieval over text, code, or image embeddings with up to 3,072 dimensions. It navigates a graph with 2-bit codes and reranks the candidates. Centered INT8 or INT4 reranking supports hot memory or SSD with a byte-bounded cache. Document ANN can select compressed reranking per request. Use exact search for a reference ranking or for synthetic and hand-engineered features. Packed `u64` fingerprints use exact Hamming distance.
- **Pelorus brings the geometry of a hierarchy into the query itself.** For models that encode taxonomies, concept hierarchies, or image–text relationships in a fixed-curvature Poincaré ball, explicitly build the Pelorus index with the model's curvature magnitude `c > 0`. Stored and query coordinates must satisfy `c · ‖x‖² < 1`. Its graph navigation preserves radial information and compresses direction to 2 bits per coordinate. Candidates can be reranked in hot memory, from a memory mapping, or from SSD. Set `exact: true` for an exhaustive geodesic search over the stored coordinates.

With a Pelorus index built on two-dimensional embeddings, this TQL query runs ANN search for five neighbors within the `taxonomy` graph. Membership is applied before top-K selection. The vector SDK returns geodesic distance, smallest first. TQL exposes its negative through `similarity(_)`, so higher scores are closer.

```sql
GRAPH {graph_ids: ['taxonomy']}
SEARCH PELORUS {vector: [0.12, 0.0], options: {top_k: 5}}
RETURN _.id AS id, similarity(_) AS score
ORDER BY score DESC, id
```

Rust exposes `search_pelorus` and `search_pelorus_batch`. Python uses `pelorus_request` and Node.js uses `pelorusRequest`. For document or passage retrieval, set `pelorus: true` on a `search_vector` or `search_hybrid` document request to use the same geometry.

In the standalone Pelorus benchmark on MERU-1M (one million 512-dimensional native hyperbolic embeddings), Pelorus reached 99.25% Recall@10 at 2,547 queries/s on one thread and 53,483 queries/s on 24 threads on AMD EPYC 9654. [Pelorus paper and measurements](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.22159v1)

## Documents, graphs, and storage

- **Document evidence.** Index source revisions and logical blocks, retrieve passages by text, vector, or hybrid rank, and map phrase and proximity matches back to source spans. Staged publication supports large documents.
- **Graphs and text.** Follow directed, labeled edges or use shortest paths, PageRank, Leiden communities, and personalized graph diffusion (SA-PPR). For text, BM25 ranks terms and Aho-Corasick matches registered keywords.
- **Indexed predicates.** Hash, Ordered ART, Composite ART, and Roaring Bitmap indexes accelerate equality, range, prefix, and set predicates over JSON properties.
- **Persistence and resource budgets.** Vector, payload, and graph mutations share transactions and a write-ahead log. Rom packs vectors and payloads into the main data file. Mmap maps vector and payload files separately. A shared `ResourceRuntime` budgets memory and workers across instances. Directory snapshots support backup and restore.

## Documentation

- [English overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/README_EN.md) and [Chinese overview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/README.md) cover installation and examples.
- [API reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/api-reference.md) covers Rust, Python, and Node.js configuration and return values.
- [TQL reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/tql-reference.md) covers query syntax, graph scopes, operators, and mutations.
- [QuIVer guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/quiver.md) covers dataset selection, automatic construction, reranking, and SSD I/O.
- [Pelorus guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/pelorus.md) covers index construction, curvature, batch and exact search, document queries, and residency settings.
- [Document retrieval](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/documents.md) and [named graphs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/named-graphs.md) describe evidence spans and graph membership.
- [Features](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/features.md) and [best practices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/best-practices.md) cover the data model and application design.
- [Resource runtime](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/resource-runtime.md) and [lifecycle and snapshots](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/master/docs/lifecycle-snapshots.md) cover budgets, shutdown, backup, and restore.
- [Stable release 0.9.3](https://github.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/releases/tag/v0.9.3) and its [bilingual release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Astrmira/TriviumDB/v0.9.3/docs/changes/0.9.3.md) cover compatibility and upgrades.
